held.reason: The anchor combines a distance term with a root glossed as “pass/surpass,” but the proposed backtranslation explicitly keeps two readings (“far away, beyond” and “farther than”). That does not establish the exact comparative relation needed here. Keep the exact source span in English while retaining the already-localized frequency clause and all surrounding wording. This is a bounded term hold, not a hold on the full sentence.

The wording may express the activities’ periods meeting or coinciding, but the evidence supplied does not establish that it means partial overlap rather than their happening at the same time. That distinction is the reason the exact English sentence replaced the inherited “at the same time” wording. Preserve the exact English anchor and the localized ordinary clauses until a source-backed Sesotho wording distinguishes overlap from identical timing.
